source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC-Web -> Overview.
2. Check Firmware information.
3. Click "View more" to check.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: All information should match SPEC definition.

deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL pretty-printed JSON from /redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory (firmware list) so user confirms the BMC web "firmware information" page shows the correct data. No RISK (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES identifies the standard FirmwareInventory collection but a collection response may contain only member links, not every member's component/version/state data. It bypasses Overview and `View more`, does not define the required components or active/inactive/staged semantics, disables TLS verification and places credentials in the command line; `No RISK` ignores adjacent update controls.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly adds component identity, version/state semantics, freshness, UI/API mapping and update-control exclusion. This review adds collection-member traversal, component-instance/slot binding, explicit version-normalization rules and a strict distinction between inventory observation and any update/activation action.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 853/2291 accepts a direct collection dump as agent-runnable evidence and does not verify collection members, the `View more` path, required component completeness, activation state or safe separation from update controls.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1016 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves Overview and View-more; ED-34 treats component/version expectations as Project readiness; ED-35 rejects API collection output as equivalent to UI and full component coverage; ED-38 forbids unapproved firmware/update actions, requires no automatic retry and keeps the verdict engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Verify that the BMC Overview Firmware information summary and its `View more` detail view list every Project-required firmware component instance with the correct displayed version and state according to the authoritative Project SPEC.
original_method: Capture the firmware summary on the identified BMC WebUI, open `View more` once without activating any update control, and collect the complete displayed inventory. Traverse the read-only FirmwareInventory collection and required member resources, bind each member to its actual component/slot/role, and compare UI plus API evidence to the approved component/version/state matrix.
manual_activity: The Project engineer defines which firmware-bearing components and instances must appear, their approved versions and how active, backup, staged or pending states are judged. Automation can collect and reconcile the read-only UI/API inventory, while ambiguous vendor naming and the final result remain engineer-owned.
required_inputs: Exact BMC endpoint/certificate, controller identity, firmware and WebUI build
Signed component matrix containing target type, physical/logical instance, slot/role, expected version, active/inactive/backup/staged state and permitted display normalization
Expected Overview summary fields, `View more` selector/route, role visibility and loading-complete behavior
Vendor Redfish FirmwareInventory/OEM mapping including collection member traversal, component identifiers, related-item/device links and version/state meanings
Inventory freshness rule and treatment for duplicate, absent, unexpected, pending-activation, rollback and non-updateable entries
Protected browser/API authentication, sensitive version/asset redaction, update-control exclusion and accidental-action recovery
safety_requirements: Keep the entire testcase read-only. Do not upload an image, select a file, invoke SimpleUpdate/MultipartPush/StartUpdate, activate, reset, reboot, roll back or change firmware policy.
Treat `/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` as a collection entry point; follow each required member URI and do not assume the collection envelope alone contains component versions or state.
Do not compare version strings without binding component type and instance. Identical versions can belong to different targets, and active, backup or staged images are not interchangeable.
Do not use `curl -k` or exposed command-line credentials in the formal method. Validate the intended BMC certificate and use protected authentication.
Do not clear dmesg, syslog, SEL, update or audit logs; preserve them and record inventory freshness without triggering a refresh unless a separate approved operation exists.

Navigate once and stop without automatic retry if an update control is invoked, a task is created, inventory state/timestamp unexpectedly changes, UI/API identities disagree or component mapping is ambiguous.
agent_execution_scope: Confirm the target BMC and current absence of active update tasks before entering the read-only firmware-information views.
Capture Overview first and then `View more`; enumerate every visible component, version, state, instance and detail indicator without activating adjacent controls.
GET the FirmwareInventory collection and each mapped member through trusted read-only access, correlate related items/OEM identifiers and compare against the approved matrix.
Report per-component exact, missing, extra, duplicate, stale, staged and state-mismatch outcomes; preserve update/audit logs and never issue DUT PASS/FAIL or retry automatically.
engineer_actions: Approve the complete component-instance/version/state matrix, permitted string normalization and whether inactive, backup, staged or pending entries are required or prohibited.
Approve the vendor mapping from UI entries to FirmwareInventory/OEM members, freshness contract and evidence redaction.
Review the component-by-component comparison and proof that no update/activation occurred, then issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The collection GET is a valid discovery step on implementations that expose it, but it may return only member references and cannot by itself prove the Overview/View-more rendering or complete component/version/state match. Its insecure TLS and credential handling are unacceptable for the formal procedure.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Over trusted TLS with protected authentication, GET FirmwareInventory, enumerate its Members and GET each Project-required member plus approved OEM detail. Separately capture the Overview and View-more inventory and join records by engineer-approved component/instance identity before comparing versions and states.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Overview, `View more`, all-information SPEC criterion, absent Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; the API remains supplemental read-only evidence and does not authorize UpdateService actions.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a deterministic component-instance inventory from UI summary/detail and traversed Redfish members, normalize versions only by signed rules, classify lifecycle state explicitly and compare the full set against Project SPEC with no update requests.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact BMC, platform topology, firmware/WebUI build and UpdateService implementation selected by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, UpdateService/FirmwareInventory schema types and UI build because inventory fields and OEM mappings vary by version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: DMTF Redfish UpdateService/SoftwareInventory data model, vendor firmware inventory mapping and signed Project firmware bill of materials/version matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Retains both UI checkpoints, expands a collection-envelope dump into member-level component evidence and makes activation/state semantics explicit while keeping the test read-only.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A collection GET alone may prove only discoverability; UI version text alone cannot prove component identity or activation state; version agreement does not prove every firmware region or image content is correct.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Target identity, component matrix, UI/API/OEM mapping, lifecycle-state rules, normalization, freshness, credentials and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware pages co-locate high-impact controls; cached inventory can be stale; duplicate component names, banks or slots can create false matches; some firmware may be reported outside FirmwareInventory.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a vendor inventory utility/API or additional authoritative sources when FirmwareInventory is incomplete, but must retain Overview and View-more coverage, record each tool/source and mapping, obtain engineer approval and disclose components or firmware regions not verified. Correct version display must not be generalized into proof that every firmware region is correct.
expected_evidence: Target BMC/platform identity, trusted certificate, firmware/WebUI build and UpdateService/FirmwareInventory schema metadata
Signed firmware component-instance/version/state matrix with normalization and required/optional membership rules
Redacted Overview and View-more screenshots/DOM/routes showing full displayed inventory and page readiness
FirmwareInventory collection payload plus every required member/OEM detail with component ID, instance/slot/role, version, status, updateability, related item and freshness metadata
Per-component UI/API/SPEC comparison covering missing, extra, duplicate, inactive, backup, staged, pending and stale entries
Proof no update task, image upload, activation, reset or configuration change occurred; preserved audit evidence, limitations and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target read-only firmware information in Overview and View more. The missing component matrix and DeepSeek's incomplete API method are readiness/review defects, not contradictions in the Master source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The inventory-display purpose and UI operation are clear. Component selection, versions, lifecycle states and vendor mappings are expected Project inputs, so execution waits under PACKAGE rather than permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE, retains the collection endpoint only as discovery and adds member traversal, UI preservation, component identity/state semantics and safe credential/TLS handling.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its hybrid inventory matrix and update-control boundary while adding precise collection/member completeness, instance binding and no automatic refresh/re-read behavior.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces direct-run reliance on a collection dump with UI plus member-level evidence and explicit Project-owned acceptance.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a list of member links, an unbound version string or a staged image from being accepted as the complete active firmware inventory, and prevents read-only review from drifting into firmware update execution.
independent_technical_reasoning: Firmware identity is a tuple of component, instance and lifecycle state, not a version string alone. Redfish inventory is collection-based and often requires member/OEM traversal, while the WebUI may merge or suppress entries. A correct SIT comparison therefore verifies set completeness and per-entry identity across summary, detail, API and SPEC, with update controls treated as an explicit hazard outside this row.
